glosses: marks the object of liking, ability, or perception
patterns.usage_note: が marks what a stative predicate is about: the thing liked, understood, needed, wanted, seen or heard (日本語が分かる, 水が飲みたい, 音が聞こえる), where English would use a direct object. Its siblings are the plain subject marker (雨が降る) and the clause-linking が meaning but (高いが買った). を does turn up with 〜たい and with some potentials when the action itself is in focus, but が is the default in short clauses.

examples.ruby: 帰[かえ]り道[みち]で、とにかく冷[つめ]たい水[みず]が飲[の]みたかった。
examples.english: On the walk home, all I wanted was a drink of cold water.

examples.ruby: 弟[おとうと]は昔[むかし]から蜘蛛[くも]が苦手[にがて]らしい。
examples.english: My little brother has apparently always been squeamish about spiders.

examples.ruby: 祖父[そふ]は今[いま]でも細[こま]かい字[じ]がよく見[み]えるらしい。
examples.english: My grandfather can still make out fine print perfectly well, it seems.
